sections.overview: Labeo ruddi Boulenger, 1907 is a currently recognized freshwater cyprinid species in the genus Labeo.
sections.identification: It reaches about 30 centimetres standard length and has 12–13 soft rays in the dorsal fin.
sections.habitat: It favours warm, quiet or standing water in middle- and lowveld rivers, especially deep pools over muddy bottoms.
sections.diet: FishBase describes it as feeding on organic sediments.
sections.behavior: During the rainy season it moves upstream through swollen rivers to breed.
sections.reproduction: The documented upstream movement is associated with breeding, but detailed spawning biology remains poorly documented.
sections.ecology: It shares the genus Labeo with L. rosae and L. altivelis; the 2025 phylogenomic study cautions that older morphological groupings of African Labeo do not consistently represent evolutionary lineages.
sections.conservation: The IUCN lists it as globally Data Deficient, reflecting insufficient information to determine extinction risk.
